title: Treasury Note on the Assessment and Settlement of Early Withdrawal Penalties, Certificates of Deposit
content:
Where a withdrawal from a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line before maturity is not of a kind that escapes a penalty, a penalty is assessed against the certificate and settled out of it.

## 1. Clauses superseded

Three clauses of this note are **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which such a penalty is worked out. They are registered here so that the subject matter they governed remains traceable against this note, and they are not to be applied:

- the clause fixing the sum the penalty is charged on as the principal the request removes, namely the sum requested for a partial withdrawal and the whole principal balance after accrued interest is credited for a full one — **no longer in force**;
- the clause fixing the penalty as that sum multiplied by the interest rate, divided by one hundred, multiplied by the penalty days and divided by the days in the year, rounded to the nearest cent with a half rounded up — **no longer in force**;
- the clause fixing the penalty days as the days the tier publishes, save that on principal taken out within six calendar days of funding they became the greater of the days the tier publishes and the tier's smallest penalty in those opening days — **no longer in force**.

The tier figures those clauses referred to remain valid and are published on the Treasury schedule of early withdrawal penalties for this line.

## 2. The penalty reaches principal

The penalty is taken out of principal even where it comes to more than the interest the certificate has earned, every tier of this line permitting the penalty to reach principal. An owner may therefore receive back less than they placed.

## 3. Settlement of the withdrawal

| Withdrawal | Sum paid out to the owner | Effect of the penalty | Standing of the certificate afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| full, before maturity | the principal balance less the penalty | taken from the balance before payment | closed |
| partial, before maturity | the sum requested | deducted from the principal that remains | open for the rest of the term |

So on a full withdrawal the owner receives the balance net of the penalty and nothing remains; on a partial the owner receives exactly what was asked for, and it is the principal left behind that bears the penalty.

superseded_clauses: The penalty basis is the principal the request removes: the requested amount for a partial, and the whole principal_balance after crediting accrued interest for a full withdrawal.
The penalty equals the penalty basis times interest_rate divided by 100 times penalty_days divided by day_count_basis, rounded half-up to the cent.

penalty_days is early_withdrawal_penalty_days, except that on principal withdrawn within six calendar days after funding it is the greater of early_withdrawal_penalty_days and first_six_days_minimum_penalty_days on every tier.
